We aim to study six N-bearing species: methyl cyanide (CH$_3$CN), isocyanic acid (HNCO), formamide (NH$_2$CHO), ethyl cyanide (C$_2$H$_5$CN), vinyl cyanide (C$_2$H$_3$CN) and methylamine (CH$_3$NH$_2$) in a large sample of line-rich high-mass protostars.
Next, we fit their spectra and find column densities and excitation temperatures of the N-bearing species mentioned above, in addition to methanol (CH$_3$OH) to be used as a reference species.

In this work we use the data from the ALMA Evolutionary study of High Mass Protocluster Formation in the Galaxy (ALMAGAL) survey (2019.1.00195.L; PI: Sergio Molinari) to do such a chemistry analysis on a large sample of high-mass sources.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00195.L.
This work uses the archival data observed by ALMA in Band 6 (${\sim 1}$ mm) as part of the ALMAGAL survey (2019.1.00195.L; PIs: P. Schilke, S. Molinari, C. Battersby, P. Ho).
Two spectral windows are used for each source with frequencies of ${\sim} 217.00-218.87$ GHz and ${\sim} 219.07-220.95$ GHz.
The spectral resolution of the data used here is ${\sim 0.7}$ km s$^{-1}$.
The frequency setting covers transitions of many N-bearing species such as CH$_{3}$CN 12$_K$-11$_K$ for $K$ going from 0 to 11.
The isotopologues of the most abundant and bright species such as HNCO, CH$_3$CN and CH$_3$OH are also considered for a more accurate derivation of the column densities of the main isotopologues.

Moreover, the column density of methanol is found from CH$_3^{18}$OH when possible (the lines are detected and not too blended) and otherwise the $^{13}$CH$_3$OH isotopologue is used (the same approach as (cite: vanGelder2022)).
From the ALMA Evolutionary study of High Mass Protocluster Formation in the Galaxy survey, 37 of the most line-rich hot molecular cores with ${\sim} 1\ensuremath{''}$ angular resolution are selected.

We consider the pipeline calibrated product data of the sources that were publicly available by 19$^{\rm th}$ of June 2021 and had beam sizes between 0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ and 1.5$\ensuremath{''}$ (${\sim} 1000-5000$ au for sources at a few kpc).
This work uses the archival data observed by ALMA in Band 6 (${\sim 1}$ mm) as part of the ALMAGAL survey (2019.1.00195.L; PIs: P. Schilke, S. Molinari, C. Battersby, P. Ho).
The targeted sources are chosen based on the sources observed in the *Herschel* Hi-Gal survey ((cite: Molinari2010); (cite: Elia2017; Elia2021)).

In this work we use the data from the ALMA Evolutionary study of High Mass Protocluster Formation in the Galaxy (ALMAGAL) survey (2019.1.00195.L; PI: Sergio Molinari) to do such a chemistry analysis on a large sample of high-mass sources.
